notes.title: Update to SpacePort Demo released.
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

Finally, an update to[b][i] SpacePort Demo[/i][/b] is here! We are pleased to announce that the free demo of our upcoming spaceflight module [i][b]SpacePort[/b][/i] for FSX and P3D series simulators has just been uploaded to our [url=http://www.terrabuilder.com/TB/fsx-spaceport.html]Web Site[/url]!

To download, please go to our [url=http://www.terrabuilder.com/TB/fsx-spaceport.html]Web Site[/url] or directly to our [url=http://www.terrabuilder.com/TB/download.html]downloads page[/url] and download "SpacePortDemo.exe" (256 Mb). The installer detects versions of the simulator (currently supporting FSX:SP2, FSX:SE, P3Dv4.x and P3Dv5.x) and if you have multiple simulator installs, you can choose for which versions you want to install.

Also, we have released an accompanying PhotoRealistic scenery of [i][b]Kennedy Space Center[/b][/i] area, that goes along with the active 3D infrastructure included in the main SpacePortDemo package. It can also be downloaded from the above links, and it is 1.39Gb in size.

A few notes on the SpacePortDemo package:
[list]
[*] SpacePortDemo will be installed to only one (user-chosen) location, and all the platforms that are using it will be referring to it.
[*] For P3Dx.x platforms, the installation is fairly benign and un-intrusive, thanks to the LM's super friendly and simple add-on installation scheme. The only things added to the P3Dvx.x is an entry to add-ons.xml, and a few settings overridden in P3D.CFG file (things like default ATC, traffic disabled, virtual copilot disabled, aircraft-specific warnings disabled, etc.). There is an installer option to save the copy of the P3D.CFG file before any changes are made, so that if anything goes wrong, you can revert back to the original P3D.CFG.
[*] For FSX:x platforms, the installation is a bit more involved. There are content entries added to FSX.CFG, DLL.XML and Scenery.CFG. As with the P3D install, backups of those 3 files will also be created so that the user can safely revert to the state of the sim before SpacePortDemo. Also, as with P3D install, there are entries changed in FSX.CFG, and in addition, there are FLT files copied to user directory, and some content (effects, bitmaps, sounds) copied to the FSX:x install directory. These files are automatically removed upon in-installation of SpacePortDemo.
[*] For FSX.x platforms, first time you run the simulator, you will have to acknowledge 1 main app and 8 new gauge DLL security permissions (P3D does not have this requirement). You will have to do this only once, and the DLL's will be listed as "friendly" in the FSX.CFG.
[*] Since there is no way we can check and cover all the possible ways users have configured their simulator platform(s) (especially the add-ons they are using), we have tested the SpacePortDemo on clean installs of all the FSX:x and P3Dvx.x versions. If things are not working, please disable all the add-ons you are using in the simulator and try again. We have, through the course of the development, found that some third-party add-ons grossly misbehave in the execution of their code and the cleanup of their content. For example, we've found that VRS's TacPack promptly deletes ALL the spawned AI objects (not just the ones it spawns) above certain altitude, rendering SpacePortDemo unusable (as you can imagine).
[*] We'd love it if you would report on problems and overall experience you are having during installation and usage of SpacePort demo - it helps us improving our product and making user experience more enjoyable. As for bugs and features, we are aware of some of them, but feel free to report any minor or major showstoppers.
[*] SpacePortDemo works best with P3Dv4.5 (version we did most testing on). P3Dv5.5 has some issues with the menu/UI system we're looking into, and a few other minor hiccups, such as going into "pause" mode upon starting or reloading of the flight. FSX:x version is showing its age and is generally slower - especially with a lot of smoke effects (rocket smoke trails and plumes) because this portion of the sim wasn't optimized as well as the P3D versions.
[*] As with real spaceflight, the GNC (Guidance, Navigation and Control) is fully automated, meaning, the launch is a "ride" that astronauts are monitoring all the way into orbit. This means that the launch in the demo FLT has pre-set orbital parameters. However, these parameters are specified in SpacePort-specific CFG files and can easily be changed by the user. The guidance at this stage of development is in its "pseudo" mode, meaning, it is only partially functional. Nonetheless, it will get you into orbit every single time you launch. SpacePort is a complex spaceflight environment consisting of many new "moving parts". SpacePort development is on-going, and as we continue to expand the capabilities, we will release Software Development Kit so that the users can create their own spaceflight content and explore this new dimension of simulation.
[/list]
That's it for now. Keep watching this thread for updates on the development of this exciting new way to enjoy our simulator hobby.

Mitch
SpacePort development Team

notes.title: New in-sim videos of P3D version of SpacePort now available
notes.content:
[h2]Check out the newest in-sim videos of the P3D version, now on our [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/TBAdmin/videos]YouTube[/url] channel! [/h2]

We have released a batch of new in-sim videos of SpacePort's P3D version, a 64-bit version of FSX! The engine is vastly improved, the FPS has doubled to tripled, and overall, the sim behaves way smoother than the 32-bit FSX:A and FSX:SE version! 

First 7 clips are of different view point of launches. Next 2 clips are of the LAS system abort modes (pad and in-flight), and the last clip is of the full launch sequence, from pad launch to the stable orbit.

notes.title: Quick update for March
notes.content:
We are continuing with the development of remaining crucial functionality (namely, guidance), as we are still in a bit of a limbo regarding the method of publishing this title. We have also initiated discussions with Microsoft about the potential for distributing this title through XBox Live for Windows platform. Hopefully this will be resolved within the next few weeks.

Other development progress milestones:
[list]
[*] High fidelity re-entry physics, with ability to insert high-precision AOA-dependent drag and lift coefficients from NASA wind tunnel tests
[*] Localized shield heating effects and re-entry plumes
[*] Improvements to re-entry parachute sequences, with new skinned animation effects
[*] Overall engine performance improvements
[/list]

We're also working hard to improve the demo install progress and we'll have the demo update in the next few weeks. In the meantime, check out this awesome video of the SLS launch, with updated sound and visual fx:

[previewyoutube=kLF-2V4eQuc;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Quick update for October
notes.content:
As you may have heard, the publishing of "FSX: Steam Edition", which is the core product for FSX SpacePort, has reverted back from DoveTail Games to Microsoft (or more precisely, XBox Game Studios). However, currently there is no channel on Microsoft's side through which add-on developers can contact MS and ask for the permission to publish add-ons for FSX:SE, such was the case when DoveTail Games was the publisher. 

This leaves us in a bit of a holding pattern with regards to the release of FSX SpacePort. We have several fallback options, which would force us to move FSX SpacePort away from Steam, but we will wait for a bit and see if MS sorts this issue out.

In the mean time, we are busy with polishing the sim and adding functionality, and we'll be shortly releasing an update to the demo showcasing this!

notes.title: Calling for pre-beta testers (mostly issues with installer)!
notes.content:
Hi everyone! We are happy to announce that we have wrapped up the work on the installer and we'll be ready in a few days (or even hours) for the demo release. We tested it as much as we could on our side, however, we'd like to have some of the public have a go at it before we release it to the world - just to shake out any problems we haven't anticipated on our end. 

With that in mind, and if you'd like to help us with this, please send a request to [u]support@terrabuilder.com[/u] with a subject line "FSX SpacePort Demo pre-release beta test". We will e-mail you a private link where you'll be able to download the FSX SpacePort demo. 

The only pre-requisite is that you have [b]FSX:(Plain, Gold, or Acceleration)[/b] or [b]FSX:Steam Edition[/b] installed and working. Also, we tested extensively on a CLEAN FSX install, so if you have a lot of third party add-ons and content, there may potentially be problems. It is obviously impossible to test with every permutation of add ons there are out there, so we'd like to hear from you if there are any problems with other DLC or add ons you may have. 

Also, please note that, if you request to be a pre-beta tester:
[list]
[*] the installer transfers files, makes registry changes and inserts entries and edits to a few configuration files. This is what every installer does, and you should be ok with that - please read and agree with EULA.
[*] we will send you the download link for the demo [u]when it is ready[/u]. There is no need to ask us subsequently for it - you will be added to our list and rest assured, demo link will be sent to you.
[*] if any problems should arise, you agree to promptly communicate with us the nature of the problem, and relay content of any error message the installer may display.
[*] if any problems are reported to us, we may ask you to take some simple remedial steps on your end. You should be familiar on how to search for and edit configuration text files.
[*] if you own a Prepar3D (P3D) version and would still like to test FSX SpacePort Demo, please let us know. We haven't tested on P3D at all (we don't own a copy), but we don't see a reason why it wouldn't be compatible. We will, however, need info on where P3D stores files (support file locations) and a few registry entry values, so you should be fairly technically apt and prepared to provide us with this info.
[/list]

That's all for now - see you soon in virtual orbit!

Mitch

notes.title: Quick Progress Update
notes.content:
We have finished all of the flight components needed to release a demo, except one: A water entry effect trigger. It sounds, looks and works great in the FSX's effect editing tool, (check out the pic) but it is giving us a lot of headache when we try to properly trigger it in the simulation. It seems the effect engine is very finicky when placed close to the surface (ground or water), so we are testing different approaches as to how to best implement this. While this is not a critical component, we feel it is important to be included in the demo, because it gives such a satisfying feel to the end of the mission!

notes.title: Parachute systems
notes.content:
We are creating an extremely accurate system of parachute recovery sequence. NASA's [url=https://www.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/atoms/files/orion_parachutes.pdf]Orion Parachute System[/url] has no less than 4 parachute groups (with 11 parachutes in total) that get deployed at different phases of re-entry:

[list]
[*] Forward bay cover parachute - 3 small parachutes that help detach forward bay cover from the Orion capsule
[*] Drogue parachute - 2 larger parachutes designed for high speed deployment that slow down capsule and stabilise it at upright position
[*] Pilot parachute - 3 small parachutes that help with deployment of the main parachute
[*] Main parachute - 3 large parachutes that slow the capsule down to about 20 km/h, until the splashdown.
[/list]

As with everything, we're developing this with modularity in mind. Parachute object is a stand-alone physics body that has its own physics attributes defined through CFG text file. So, if you feel creative, you'll be able to design your own parachutes AND write scripts for their deployment!

Check out the screen shot of the Orion's main parachute, a part of the parachute system we're developing:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31785945/b59aaaf36b6432c21bf818a2638c208219584fbe.jpg[/img]


Mitch
Lead Developer
[url=www.terrabuilder.com]TerraBuilder[/url]

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
It's been a while since we posted an update, so here's a quick one. As you are probably aware, the development is progressing at a steady but SLOW pace - we've ran into some unanticipated hurdles, mostly dealing with complexities of astrodynamics and related physics. It is, after all, rocket science ːsteamhappyː

However, I'm happy to say that most of them have now been resolved. The only thing left to resolve are recovery dynamics (physics of parachute deployment) and the physics of splashdown buoyancy (yes, we could have just plopped down the capsule into the ocean straight and level, but our physics library handles buoyancy very nicely, so we decided to add that into the feature set for the demo)

Also - the proper installer is almost done! With all this in place, we will soon have a limited feature FREE demo that will take the user through the full rocket launch sequence, orbit, de-orbit and splash down!

The only thing that will be missing is the proper automated guidance module - user will have to manually steer the rocket to a desired orbit. But no worries, we've made a slew of new MFD modes that will guide you to a nice, steady orbit with great precision - it will just require a bit of manual pitch control to get it just right!

We do apologise for the delay and truly appreciate your continued support! Hang in, we're almost there!

Mitch
Lead developer
[url=www.terrabuilder.com]TerraBuilder[/url]

notes.title: Progress update for September
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

With the summer, and a lengthy pause (vacation ːsteamboredː ) behind us, we are making steady progress towards the release date, although a few "gotchas" within the FSX engine set us back considerably. We are working on these and it looks like we'll be soon able to overcome FSX's somewhat limiting sound engine and have a custom sound layer on top of it.

In the mean time, we updated a whole lot of visuals - namely, we have a new SLS Launch Umbilical Tower (LUT) and Mobile Launch Platform (MLP) with moving parts, and they look amazing! We'll soon post screenshots/videos of the launch with the new, accurate structures - stay tuned!
